TestCases.Feature: Independent control register for each GPIO
TestCases.Test Description: Verifies default reset values and masked read/write behavior on all per-pin GPIO control and related group/interrupt registers. For each register, the expected read-back is derived from write masks and reset values; any mismatch increments failure counters and fails the test.
TestCases.Remarks: Per-pin input status can float high if not driven; forcing it low may alter selection logic, leading to default-value mismatches. Group VRW registers are intentionally skipped based on skip arrays. Non-readable or non-writable registers are conditionally skipped per mask arrays.
TestCases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry point
1) Start: test case entry.
Default-value verification (per-pin and group/interrupt registers)
2) For each register in the defined list (49 total per configuration arrays): if the reset-skip flag is set, skip this register.
3) If the read mask for the register is zero, skip reading this register.
4) Read the register.
5) Apply a mask that ignores the input status least significant bit before comparison.
6) Compare the masked value against the corresponding reset value; on mismatch, record a default-value failure.
Masked write/read verification (six data patterns)
7) For each of the six data patterns in order: 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000:
8) For every register in the list: if the write-skip flag is set, skip this register.
9) If the write mask is zero, skip writing this register.
10) Write the register with the pattern masked by the register’s write mask.
11) For the same register set: if the write-skip flag is set, skip this register.
12) If the write mask is zero, skip this register.
13) If the read mask is zero, skip this register.
14) Read the register and mask the value using the read mask.
15) Compute the expected value as the bitwise OR of: (pattern AND read mask AND write mask) with (bitwise NOT of write mask AND read mask AND reset value).
16) Compare the read value to the expected value; on mismatch, record a write/read failure.
Completion
17) If any default-value or write/read failures were recorded, the test fails; otherwise the test passes.
TestCases.Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass when: (a) every readable register’s masked value after reset matches its documented reset value; and (b) for all writable and readable registers, the read-back equals the logical combination of written bits per write mask and preserved bits from reset per write mask complement. Any mismatch causes failure.

TestCases.Feature: Independent GPIO control Register: neie (Negative edge interrupt enable)
TestCases.Test Description: Configures all pads as inputs with negative-edge interrupt enabled, generates a falling edge per pad using an external drive, waits with a bounded timeout for the ISR to assert, and validates input level, per-pin raw status, group masked status, and system interrupt clears.
TestCases.Remarks: A pre-clear of the raw group status is performed before each iteration. The wait is armed before edge generation to avoid a race. Bounded wait with a fixed retry budget ensures no infinite hangs. The ISR uses the current loop index value to validate and clear per-pin and group statuses.
TestCases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and interrupt routing
1) Start: test case entry; clear local error counter.
2) Enable the appropriate interrupt at the interrupt controller (instance-dependent).
3) Enable the system-level interrupt output for the selected GPIO instance in the system register INTR_EN1.
Pad drive to known level and per-pin configuration
4) Drive the pad driver register at 0xA0243ffc to all-high to establish a known level.
5) For each pad index from 0 to 31: write the per-pin control register at GP0_GPIO_8 + (index * 4) to set input mode, enable negative-edge interrupt, and clear any latched raw status; wait for 10 time units after each configuration.
Per-iteration interrupt enable, edge generation, and wait
6) For each bit position from 0 to 31:
7) Clear the corresponding group raw status bit by writing 1 to the RAW_STCLR1 register for that bit.
8) Enable only this bit in the group enable register GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1; wait for 10 time units.
9) Arm the interrupt-wait latch prior to stimulus.
10) Re-drive the pad driver register to all-high, wait 30 time units, then drive it with the target bit forced low to create a single falling edge on the current pad.
11) Enter a bounded wait loop with a starting timeout count of 5000; in each iteration wait 10 time units and exit when the ISR latch is cleared or when the timeout expires.
12) If the timeout expires, record an error for this pad.
ISR behavior and validation (executed upon interrupt)
13) On ISR entry: compute the current bit mask from the active index; clear the wait latch to release the main thread.
14) Drive the pad driver back to all-high (known state) to avoid retriggering.
15) Read the per-pin control/status register for the active pad; verify the input status bit indicates low following a falling edge; on mismatch, record an error.
16) Verify the per-pin raw status bit is set; if set: read the group masked status register GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and confirm the active bit is set; otherwise record an error.
17) Clear the per-pin raw status by writing the per-pin control register with input mode and the raw clear bit set.
18) Clear the corresponding bit in the RAW_STCLR1 register (write-one-to-clear at group level).
19) Re-read the group masked status register and confirm it is zero; on mismatch, record an error.
20) Clear the corresponding system-level raw status in RAW_STCR1 for the selected GPIO instance and clear the controller interrupt.
Completion
21) After all iterations complete, finish with the accumulated error count.
TestCases.Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass when, for each pad: the interrupt is observed before the timeout; the input bit reads low after the falling edge; the masked group status bit for that pad is set during service and reads zero after per-pin and group clears; the system raw interrupt clear removes the corresponding source; and the final result indicates zero errors.

TestCases.Feature: Independent GPIO control Register: peie (Positive edge interrupt enable)
TestCases.Test Description: Enables positive-edge interrupt on all pads, configures pads as inputs via group IO control, enables group interrupt, then for each pad generates a rising edge and waits for the ISR to occur within a bounded timeout. The ISR validates group masked status, clears per-pin raw status across all pads, confirms group clear, and clears the system raw interrupt.
TestCases.Remarks: Wait is armed before creating the rising edge to avoid missed interrupts. During service, the group enable is masked to avoid re-entry, per-pin raw is cleared with write-one-to-clear across all pads, and system raw status is verified cleared before re-enabling group interrupt.
TestCases.Test Steps / Procedure:
Entry and interrupt routing
1) Start: test case entry and local error counter init.
2) Enable the target interrupt at the interrupt controller (instance-dependent).
3) Enable the corresponding system-level interrupt in INTR_EN1.
Per-pin positive-edge enable and group IO control
4) For each pad index from 0 to 31: write the per-pin control register at GP0_GPIO_8 + (index * 4) to enable positive-edge interrupt.
5) Wait 10 time units.
6) Configure pad groups to input mode by writing 0xFF to GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4 (group masks set for all eight pads per group).
7) Wait 10 time units.
Group interrupt enable and per-pad stimulation loop
8) Enable all 32 pad interrupts in GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 by writing all ones.
9) For each pad index from 0 to 31:
10) Drive the pad driver (0xA0243ffc) low; wait 10 time units.
11) Arm the ISR wait latch and then drive the pad driver high to create a single rising edge on the active pad.
12) Enter a bounded wait with timeout count of 2000; in each iteration wait 10 time units; if the ISR latch does not clear before timeout, record an error and exit the loop.
13) Optionally restore low level and wait 10 time units before the next iteration.
ISR behavior and validation (executed upon interrupt)
14) Compute the bit mask from the current pad index and clear the ISR wait latch.
15) Read group masked status GP0_INTR1_INTR_STS1 and temporarily mask GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 to 0 to avoid re-entry.
16) If any group bit is set, consider the group interrupt as observed; else record an error.
17) For each pad index from 0 to 31: clear per-pin raw status by writing the raw-clear bit in each per-pin control register.
18) Wait 2 time units.
19) Re-read group masked status and expect zero; on mismatch, record an error.
20) Clear the system raw interrupt in RAW_STCR1 and verify it is cleared by reading back; on mismatch, record an error.
21) Re-enable GP0_INTR1_INTR_EN1 with all ones and clear the controller interrupt.
Completion
22) Finish with the accumulated error count.
TestCases.Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass when for each iteration the interrupt arrives before timeout; the group masked status indicates an interrupt during service and reads zero after per-pin and group clears; the system raw interrupt is cleared as verified by read-back; and the overall error counter is zero at test completion.
